sentences.zh: 漢因秦制，帝之祖母曰太皇太后，母曰皇太后，妃曰皇后，餘則多稱夫人，隨世增損，非如《周禮》有夫人、嬪婦、御妻之數焉。

translations.literal: Han followed Qin institutions: the emperor's grandmother was called Grand Empress Dowager, his mother Empress Dowager, his consort Empress; the rest were mostly called Lady, increased or reduced with the age—not like the Zhou Rites' fixed numbers of ladies, consorts, wives, and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Han followed Qin institutions: the emperor's grandmother was called grand empress dowager, his mother empress dowager, his consort empress; the rest were mostly called lady, increased or reduced with the times—not like the fixed numbers of ladies, consorts, wives, and attendants in the Zhou Rites.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉相因，時有升降，前史言之具矣。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin followed one another, with promotions and demotions from time to time; earlier histories have stated this fully.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin followed one another, with titles rising and falling from time to time; earlier histories have stated this fully.

sentences.zh: 魏氏王業之兆，雖始於神元，然自昭成之前，未具言六宮之典；

translations.literal: Though the Wei royal enterprise began with Shenyuan, before Zhaocheng the regulations of the six palaces were not fully set forth;
translations.idiomatic: Though the Wei royal enterprise began with Shenyuan, before Zhaocheng the regulations of the six palaces were not fully set forth;

sentences.zh: 而章、平、思、昭、穆、惠、煬、烈八帝妃後無聞。

translations.literal: and of the eight emperors Zhang, Ping, Si, Zhao, Mu, Hui, Yang, and Lie, the consorts are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: and of the eight emperors Zhang, Ping, Si, Zhao, Mu, Hui, Yang, and Lie, the consorts are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 道武追尊祖妣，皆從帝諡為皇后。

translations.literal: Daowu posthumously honored his ancestresses, all taking the emperor's posthumous title as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu posthumously honored his ancestresses, all taking the emperor's posthumous title as empress.

sentences.zh: 始立中宮，餘妾或稱夫人，多少無限，然皆有品次。

translations.literal: He first established the central palace; other concubines might be called lady, without limit in number, yet all had grades.
translations.idiomatic: He first established the central palace; other concubines might be called lady, without limit in number, yet all had grades.

sentences.zh: 太武稍增左右昭儀及貴人、椒房等，後庭漸已多矣。

translations.literal: Taiwu gradually added left and right zhaoyi and noble ladies, pepper chambers, and the like; the rear apartments grew numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu gradually added left and right zhaoyi, noble ladies, pepper chambers, and the like; the rear apartments grew numerous.

sentences.zh: 又魏故事，將立皇后，必令手鑄金人，以成者為吉，不則不得立也。

translations.literal: Again, by Wei precedent, when about to establish an empress, she had to cast a golden figure by hand—success was auspicious, otherwise she could not be established.
translations.idiomatic: Again, by Wei precedent, when about to establish an empress, she had to cast a golden figure by hand—success was auspicious, otherwise she could not be established.

sentences.zh: 又太武、文成，保母劬勞之恩，並極尊崇之義，雖事乖典禮，而觀過知仁。

translations.literal: Again, for Taiwu and Wencheng, the toil of wet-nurses was honored to the utmost—though it deviated from ritual, one may know benevolence by observing excess.
translations.idiomatic: Again, for Taiwu and Wencheng, the toil of wet-nurses was honored to the utmost—though it deviated from ritual, one may know benevolence by observing excess.

sentences.zh: 孝文改定內官：左右昭儀位視大司馬，三夫人視三公，三嬪視三卿，六嬪視六卿，世婦視中大夫，御女視元士。

translations.literal: Xiaowen reformed inner offices: left and right zhaoyi ranked with the grand marshal; three ladies with the three dukes; three pin with the three ministers; six pin with the six ministers; world wives with chief grand masters; palace women with yuan shi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen reformed inner offices: left and right zhaoyi ranked with the grand marshal; three ladies with the three dukes; three pin with the three ministers; six pin with the six ministers; world wives with chief grand masters; palace women with yuan shi.

sentences.zh: 後置女職，以典內司。

translations.literal: Later female offices were added to administer the inner bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Later female offices were added to administer the inner bureau.

sentences.zh: 內司視尚書令、僕。

translations.literal: The inner bureau ranked with the director and vice director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: The inner bureau ranked with the director and vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 作司、大監、女侍中三官視二品。

translations.literal: Director of works, grand supervisor, and female attendant-in-chief—three offices ranked as second grade.
translations.idiomatic: Director of works, grand supervisor, and female attendant-in-chief—three offices ranked as second grade.

sentences.zh: 監、女尚書、美人，女史、女賢人、女書史、書女、小書女五官視三品。

translations.literal: Supervisor, female master of writing, beauties, female scribes, female worthies, female recorders, writing women, and junior writing women—five offices ranked as third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor, female master of writing, beauties, female scribes, female worthies, female recorders, writing women, and junior writing women—five offices ranked as third grade.

sentences.zh: 中才人、供人、中使、女生才人、恭使宮人視四品。

translations.literal: Middle talents, attendants, middle envoys, palace female talents, and respectful palace women ranked as fourth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Middle talents, attendants, middle envoys, palace female talents, and respectful palace women ranked as fourth grade.

sentences.zh: 青衣、女酒、女饗、女食、奚官女奴視五品。

translations.literal: Green robes, female wine, female feast, female food, and Xian official female slaves ranked as fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Green robes, female wine, female feast, female food, and Xian official female slaves ranked as fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武、文襄，俱未踐尊極。

translations.literal: As for Qi Shenwu and Wenxiang, both had not yet reached the supreme throne.
translations.idiomatic: As for Qi Shenwu and Wenxiang, both had not yet reached the supreme throne.

sentences.zh: 神武嫡妻稱妃，其所娉蠕蠕女稱為蠕蠕公主。

translations.literal: Shenwu's principal wife was called consort; the Rouran woman he married was called Princess Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu's principal wife was called consort; the Rouran woman he married was called Princess Rouran.

sentences.zh: 文襄既尚魏朝公主，故無別號。

translations.literal: Wenxiang had married a Wei princess, hence no separate title.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang had married a Wei princess, hence no separate title.

sentences.zh: 兩宮自余姬侍，並稱娘而已。

translations.literal: In both palaces, other concubines were all called niang only.
translations.idiomatic: In both palaces, other concubines were all called niang only.

sentences.zh: 文宣後庭雖有夫人、嬪、御之稱，然未具員數。

translations.literal: Wenxuan's rear apartments had titles of lady, pin, and imperial attendant, but the quotas were not fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan's rear apartments had titles of lady, pin, and imperial attendant, but the quotas were not fixed.

sentences.zh: 孝昭內職甚少，唯楊嬪才貌兼美，復是貴家，襄城王母桑氏有德行，並蒙恩禮，其餘無聞焉。

translations.literal: Xiaozhao's inner offices were very few; only Consort Yang, with talent and beauty together, was also of a noble house; Sang, mother of the Prince of Xiangcheng, had virtue and conduct—both received favor and courtesy; the rest are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhao's inner offices were very few; only Consort Yang, with talent and beauty together, was also of a noble house; Sang, mother of the Prince of Xiangcheng, had virtue and conduct—both received favor and courtesy; the rest are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 河清新令：內命婦依古制有三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御女。

translations.literal: Heqing new statutes: inner titled ladies followed antiquity with three ladies, nine pin, twenty-seven world wives, and eighty-one palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Heqing new statutes: inner titled ladies followed antiquity with three ladies, nine pin, twenty-seven world wives, and eighty-one palace women.

sentences.zh: 又准漢制置昭儀，有左右二人，比丞相。

translations.literal: Again following Han institutions, zhaoyi were established, left and right, two persons, ranking with the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Again following Han institutions, zhaoyi were established, left and right, two persons, ranking with the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 其弘德、正德、崇德為三夫人，比三公。

translations.literal: Hongde, Zhengde, and Chongde were the three ladies, ranking with the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Hongde, Zhengde, and Chongde were the three ladies, ranking with the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 光猷、昭訓、隆徽為上嬪，比三卿。

translations.literal: Guangyou, Zhaoxun, and Longhui were upper pin, ranking with the three ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyou, Zhaoxun, and Longhui were upper pin, ranking with the three ministers.

sentences.zh: 宣徽、凝暉、宣明、順華、凝華、光訓為下嬪、比六卿。

translations.literal: Xuanhui, Ninghui, Xuanming, Shunhua, Ninghua, and Guangxun were lower pin, ranking with the six ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui, Ninghui, Xuanming, Shunhua, Ninghua, and Guangxun were lower pin, ranking with the six ministers.

sentences.zh: 正華、令側、修訓、曜儀、明淑、芳華、敬婉、昭華、光正、昭甯、貞範、弘徽、和德、弘猷、茂光、明信、靜訓、曜德、廣訓、暉範、敬訓、芳猷、婉華、明範、豔儀、暉則、敬信為二十七世婦，比從三品。

sentences.zh: 武成好內，並具其員，自外又置才人，采女，以為散號。

translations.literal: Wucheng loved the inner quarters and filled all quotas; besides these he also set talents and caicai as loose titles.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng loved the inner quarters and filled all quotas; besides these he also set talents and caicai as loose titles.

sentences.zh: 後王既立二後，昭儀以下皆倍其數。

translations.literal: Later, when the king established two empresses, below zhaoyi all numbers were doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the king established two empresses, below zhaoyi all numbers were doubled.

sentences.zh: 又置左右娥英，比左右丞相，降昭儀比二大夫。

translations.literal: Left and right Eying were also added, ranking with left and right chancellors; zhaoyi was lowered to rank with second grand masters.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right Eying were also added, ranking with left and right chancellors; zhaoyi was lowered to rank with second grand masters.

sentences.zh: 尋又置淑妃一人，比相國。

translations.literal: Soon a shufei was added, one person, ranking with the prime minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a shufei was added, one person, ranking with the prime minister.

sentences.zh: 周氏率由姬制，內職有序。

translations.literal: The Zhou followed the Ji institutions; inner offices were orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou followed the Ji institutions; inner offices were orderly.

sentences.zh: 文帝創基，修衽席以儉約；

translations.literal: Wendi in founding the state kept bed and mat frugal;
translations.idiomatic: Wendi in founding the state kept bed and mat frugal;

sentences.zh: 武皇嗣曆，節情欲於矯枉。

translations.literal: Wuhuang succeeding the throne restrained passion in correcting excess.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang succeeding the throne restrained passion in correcting excess.

sentences.zh: 宮闈有貫魚之美，戚裏無私溺之尤，可謂得君人之體也。

translations.literal: The palace had the beauty of strung fish; the imperial kin had no fault of private favoritism—this may be called grasping the ruler's substance.
translations.idiomatic: The palace had the beauty of strung fish; the imperial kin had no fault of private favoritism—this may be called grasping the ruler's substance.

sentences.zh: 宣皇外行其志，內逞其欲，溪壑難滿，采擇無厭；

translations.literal: Xuanhuang outwardly pursued his aims, inwardly indulged his desires; ravines and gullies could not be filled, selection without end;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhuang outwardly pursued his aims, inwardly indulged his desires; ravines and gullies could not be filled, selection without end;

sentences.zh: 恩之所加，莫限廝皁；

translations.literal: where favor reached, none was limited to menials;
translations.idiomatic: where favor reached, none was limited to menials;

sentences.zh: 榮之所及，無隔險詖。

translations.literal: where glory extended, none was barred by danger or flattery.
translations.idiomatic: where glory extended, none was barred by danger or flattery.

sentences.zh: 於是升蘭殿以正位，踐椒庭而齊體者，非一人焉；

translations.literal: Thus those who ascended the orchid hall for the principal place and trod the pepper courtyard as equals were not one;
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who ascended the orchid hall for the principal place and trod the pepper courtyard as equals were not one;

sentences.zh: 階房帷而拖青紫，緣恩幸而擁玉帛，非一族焉。

translations.literal: those who by the curtain dragged blue and purple and by favor clutched jade and silk were not one clan.
translations.idiomatic: those who by the curtain dragged blue and purple and by favor clutched jade and silk were not one clan.

sentences.zh: 雖辛、癸之荒淫，趙、李之傾惑，曾未足比其仿佛也。

translations.literal: Though the debauchery of Xin and Gui and the ruin wrought by Zhao and Li scarcely suffice to compare in likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Though the debauchery of Xin and Gui and the ruin wrought by Zhao and Li scarcely suffice to compare in likeness.

sentences.zh: 人厭苛政，弊事實多，文帝之祀忽諸，特由於此。

translations.literal: Men weary of harsh government; abuses were many—Wendi's sacrifices suddenly ended, especially for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Men weary of harsh government; abuses were many—Wendi's sacrifices suddenly ended, especially for this reason.

sentences.zh: 隋文思革前弊，大矯其違，唯皇后當室，傍無私寵；

translations.literal: Sui Wendi wished to reform former abuses and greatly correct their violations; only the empress held the house, with no private favorites at her side;
translations.idiomatic: Sui Wendi wished to reform former abuses and greatly correct their violations; only the empress held the house, with no private favorites at her side;

sentences.zh: 婦官位號，未詳備焉。

translations.literal: women's offices and titles were not yet fully detailed.
translations.idiomatic: women's offices and titles were not yet fully detailed.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年著內官之式，略依《周禮》，省減其數。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang the form of inner offices was set, roughly following the Zhou Rites, reducing their number.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang the form of inner offices was set, roughly following the Zhou Rites, reducing their number.

sentences.zh: 嬪三員，掌教四德，視正三品；

translations.literal: Three pin, teaching the four virtues, ranked regular third grade;
translations.idiomatic: Three pin, teaching the four virtues, ranked regular third grade;

sentences.zh: 世婦九員，掌賓客祭祀，視正五品；

translations.literal: nine world wives, managing guests and sacrifices, ranked regular fifth grade;
translations.idiomatic: nine world wives, managing guests and sacrifices, ranked regular fifth grade;

sentences.zh: 女御三十八員，掌女功絲枲，視正七品。

translations.literal: thirty-eight palace women, managing women's work and silk, ranked regular seventh grade.
translations.idiomatic: thirty-eight palace women, managing women's work and silk, ranked regular seventh grade.

sentences.zh: 又采漢、晉舊儀，置六尚、六司、六典，遞相統攝，以掌宮掖之政。

translations.literal: Again adopting Han and Jin old rites, six Shang, six Si, and six Dian were set, each supervising the next, to govern palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Again adopting Han and Jin old rites, six Shang, six Si, and six Dian were set, each supervising the next, to govern palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 一曰尚宮，掌導引皇后及閨閣稟賜。

translations.literal: First, Shang Palace, guiding the empress and inner gates' grants.
translations.idiomatic: First, Shang Palace, guiding the empress and inner gates' grants.

sentences.zh: 管司令三人，掌圖籍法式，糾察宣奏；

translations.literal: It oversaw three Ling Si, managing registers and laws, investigating and memorializing;
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw three Ling Si, managing registers and laws, investigating and memorializing;

sentences.zh: 典琮三人，掌琮璽器玩。

translations.literal: three Dian Cong, managing seals and ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: three Dian Cong, managing seals and ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 二曰尚儀，掌禮儀教學。

translations.literal: Second, Shang Ceremonial, managing ritual and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Second, Shang Ceremonial, managing ritual and instruction.

sentences.zh: 道武皇后慕容氏，寶之季女也。

translations.literal: Daowu's Empress Murong was Bao's youngest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu's Empress Murong was Bao's youngest daughter.

sentences.zh: 中山平，入充掖庭，得幸。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified she entered the rear apartments and won favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshan was pacified she entered the rear apartments and won favor.

sentences.zh: 左丞相、衛王儀等奏請立皇后。

translations.literal: Left chancellor Prince of Wei Yi and others memorialized to establish the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Left chancellor Prince of Wei Yi and others memorialized to establish the empress.

sentences.zh: 帝從儀，令后鑄金人成，乃立之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Yi; he had the empress cast a golden figure—when it succeeded, she was established.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Yi; he had the empress cast a golden figure—when it succeeded, she was established.

sentences.zh: 封后母孟為漂陽君。

translations.literal: The empress's mother Meng was enfeoffed as Lady of Piaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother Meng was enfeoffed as Lady of Piaoyang.

sentences.zh: 后崩。

translations.literal: The empress died.
translations.idiomatic: The empress died.

sentences.zh: 道武宣穆皇后劉氏，劉眷女也。

translations.literal: Daowu Xuanmu Empress Liu was Liu Juan's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu Xuanmu Empress Liu was Liu Juan's daughter.

sentences.zh: 登國初，納為夫人，生華陰公主，后生明元。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo she was taken as lady; she bore the Princess of Huayin, later Mingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo she was taken as lady; she bore the Princess of Huayin, later Mingyuan.

sentences.zh: 后專理內事，寵待有加，以鑄金人不成，故不登后位。

translations.literal: The empress managed inner affairs alone; favor was added, but because casting the golden figure failed, she did not ascend the empress seat.
translations.idiomatic: The empress managed inner affairs alone; favor was added, but because casting the golden figure failed, she did not ascend the empress seat.

sentences.zh: 魏故事，後宮產子，將為儲貳，其母皆賜死。

translations.literal: By Wei precedent, when the rear palace bore a son who would be heir, the mother was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: By Wei precedent, when the rear palace bore a son who would be heir, the mother was ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 道武末年，后以舊法薨。

translations.literal: In Daowu's last years the empress died by the old law.
translations.idiomatic: In Daowu's last years the empress died by the old law.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，追遵諡位，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, he followed and granted posthumous title and paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne, he followed and granted posthumous title and paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 自此後，宮人為帝母，皆正配饗焉。

translations.literal: From this onward, palace women who were the emperor's mother were all properly paired in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: From this onward, palace women who were the emperor's mother were all properly paired in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 明元昭哀皇后姚氏，姚興女西平長公主也。

translations.literal: Mingyuan Zhaoguai Empress Yao was Yao Xing's daughter, Princess of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan Zhaoguai Empress Yao was Yao Xing's daughter, Princess of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 明元以后納之，後為夫人。

translations.literal: Mingyuan later took her in; she became lady.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan later took her in; she became lady.

sentences.zh: 后以鑄金人不成，未升尊位，然帝寵禮如后。

translations.literal: Because casting the golden figure failed, she did not rise to supreme rank, yet the emperor favored and treated her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Because casting the golden figure failed, she did not rise to supreme rank, yet the emperor favored and treated her as empress.

sentences.zh: 是後猶欲正位，后謙不當。

translations.literal: Afterward he still wished to set her in the principal place; the empress declined as unfitting.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he still wished to set her in the principal place; the empress declined as unfitting.

sentences.zh: 泰常五年，薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taichang she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taichang she died.

sentences.zh: 帝追恨之，贈皇后璽綬而加諡焉。

translations.literal: The emperor pursued regret, bestowing empress seals and cords and adding posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pursued regret, bestowing empress seals and cords and adding posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 葬雲中金陵。

translations.literal: She was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 明元密皇后杜氏，魏郡鄴人，陽平王超之妹也。

translations.literal: Mingyuan's secret Empress Du was a man of Ye in Wei commandery, younger sister of Prince of Yangping Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan's secret Empress Du was a man of Ye in Wei commandery, younger sister of Prince of Yangping Chao.

sentences.zh: 初以良家子選入太子宮，有寵，生太武。

translations.literal: At first, as a good-family daughter she was chosen into the crown prince's palace, won favor, and bore Taiwu.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as a good-family daughter she was chosen into the crown prince's palace, won favor, and bore Taiwu.

sentences.zh: 及明元即位，拜貴嬪。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, she was made noble consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne, she was made noble consort.

sentences.zh: 泰常五年，薨，諡曰貴嬪，葬雲中金陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taichang she died; posthumous title Noble Consort; buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taichang she died; posthumous title Noble Consort; buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 太武即位，追尊號諡，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: When Taiwu took the throne, he posthumously raised title and posthumous name and paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu took the throne, he posthumously raised title and posthumous name and paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 又立廟于鄴，刺史四時薦祀。

translations.literal: A temple was also set up at Ye; the prefect presented seasonal sacrifices four times.
translations.idiomatic: A temple was also set up at Ye; the prefect presented seasonal sacrifices four times.

sentences.zh: 以魏郡，太后所生之邑，復其調役。

translations.literal: Because Wei commandery was the town where the empress dowager was born, its levies were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wei commandery was the town where the empress dowager was born, its levies were remitted.

sentences.zh: 後甘露降於廟庭。

translations.literal: Later sweet dew fell in the temple courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Later sweet dew fell in the temple courtyard.

sentences.zh: 文成時，相州刺史高閭表修后廟，詔曰：「婦人外成，理無獨祀；

translations.literal: Under Wencheng, Inspector of Xiangzhou Gao Lü memorialized to repair the empress's temple; the edict said: "Women achieve outwardly; by principle they are not sacrificed alone;
translations.idiomatic: Under Wencheng, inspector of Xiangzhou Gao Lü memorialized to repair the empress's temple; the edict said, "Women achieve outwardly; by principle they are not sacrificed alone;

sentences.zh: 陰必配陽，以成天地，未聞有莘之國立大姒之饗。

translations.literal: yin must pair with yang to complete Heaven and Earth—I have not heard of the state of Youxin establishing great sacrifices to Da Si.
translations.idiomatic: yin must pair with yang to complete Heaven and Earth—I have not heard of the state of Youxin establishing great sacrifices to Da Si.

sentences.zh: 此乃先皇所立，一時之至感，非經世之遠制，便可罷祀。

translations.literal: This was set up by the former emperor as a moment's utmost feeling, not a far-reaching institution for generations—sacrifice may be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: This was set up by the former emperor as a moment's utmost feeling, not a far-reaching institution for generations—sacrifice may be stopped."

sentences.zh: 」先是，太武保母竇氏，初以夫家坐事誅，與二女俱入宮；

translations.literal: Earlier, Taiwu's wet-nurse Lady Dou, at first because her husband's family was condemned, entered the palace with two daughters;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Taiwu's wet-nurse Lady Dou, at first because her husband's family was condemned, entered the palace with two daughters;

sentences.zh: 操行純備，進退以禮，明元命為太武保母。

translations.literal: conduct pure and complete, advancing and retreating by ritual—Mingyuan made her Taiwu's wet-nurse.
translations.idiomatic: conduct pure and complete, advancing and retreating by ritual—Mingyuan made her Taiwu's wet-nurse.

sentences.zh: 性仁慈，帝感其恩訓，奉養不異所生。

translations.literal: Kind and humane, the emperor felt her gracious teaching and supported her no differently from his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: Kind and humane, the emperor felt her gracious teaching and supported her no differently from his birth mother.

sentences.zh: 及即位，尊為皇太后，封其弟漏頭為遼東王。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, she was honored as empress dowager; her younger brother Loutou was enfeoffed Prince of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, she was honored as empress dowager; her younger brother Loutou was enfeoffed Prince of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 太后訓厘內外，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: The empress dowager instructed inside and outside with great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager instructed inside and outside with great reputation.

sentences.zh: 性恬素寡欲，喜怒不形於色，好揚人之善，隱人之過。

translations.literal: Plain and of few desires, joy and anger did not show on her face; she liked to praise others' good and hide others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and of few desires, joy and anger did not show on her face; she liked to praise others' good and hide others' faults.

sentences.zh: 帝征涼州，蠕蠕吳堤入寇，太后命諸將擊走之。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned to Liangzhou, Rouran Wuti invaded; the empress dowager ordered generals to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned to Liangzhou, Rouran Wuti invaded; the empress dowager ordered generals to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 真君元年，崩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenjun she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenjun she died.

sentences.zh: 詔天下大臨三日，太保盧魯元監護喪事，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: An edict ordered great mourning throughout the realm for three days; Grand Guardian Lu Luyuan oversaw the funeral; posthumous title Hui.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered great mourning throughout the realm for three days; Grand Guardian Lu Luyuan oversaw the funeral; posthumous title Hui.

sentences.zh: 葬崞山，從后意也。

translations.literal: Buried at Guo Mountain, following the empress dowager's wish.
translations.idiomatic: Buried at Guo Mountain, following the empress dowager's wish.

sentences.zh: 初，后嘗登崞山，顧謂左右曰：「吾母養帝躬，敬神而愛人，若死而不滅，必不為賤鬼。

translations.literal: Earlier the empress dowager had climbed Guo Mountain and said to attendants: "My mother raised the emperor's person, revering spirits and loving men—if after death she is not extinguished, she will surely not be a base ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the empress dowager had climbed Guo Mountain and said to attendants, "My mother raised the emperor's person, revering spirits and loving men—if after death she is not extinguished, she will surely not be a base ghost.

sentences.zh: 然於先朝，本無位次，不可違禮以從園陵。

translations.literal: Yet toward the former court she had no place in rank—one cannot violate ritual to follow the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet toward the former court she had no place in rank—one cannot violate ritual to follow the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 此山之上，可以終托。

translations.literal: On this mountain above, one may be finally entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: On this mountain above, one may be finally entrusted."

sentences.zh: 」故葬焉。

translations.literal: Therefore she was buried there.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore she was buried there.

sentences.zh: 別立后寢廟於崞山，建碑頌德。

translations.literal: A separate rear-chamber temple was built at Guo Mountain; a stele was erected praising virtue.
translations.idiomatic: A separate rear-chamber temple was built at Guo Mountain; a stele was erected praising virtue.

sentences.zh: 太武皇后赫連氏，屈丐女也。

translations.literal: Taiwu's Empress Helian was Qu Gui's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu's Empress Helian was Qu Gui's daughter.

sentences.zh: 太武平統萬，納后及二妹，俱為貴人，後立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Taiwu pacified Tongwan he took the empress and two younger sisters, all as noble ladies; later she was established empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu pacified Tongwan he took the empress and two younger sisters, all as noble ladies; later she was established empress.

sentences.zh: 文成初，崩，祔葬金陵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wencheng she died and was buried attached at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wencheng she died and was buried attached at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 太武敬哀皇后賀氏，代人也。

translations.literal: Taiwu Jing'ai Empress He was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu Jing'ai Empress He was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 初為夫人，生景穆。

translations.literal: At first she was lady; she bore Jingmu.
translations.idiomatic: At first she was lady; she bore Jingmu.

sentences.zh: 神蒨元年，薨，追贈貴嬪，葬雲中金陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenqi she died; posthumously made noble consort; buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenqi she died; posthumously made noble consort; buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 後追號尊諡，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: Later posthumous title and honorific were raised; paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later posthumous title and honorific were raised; paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 景穆恭皇后郁久閭氏，河東王毗妹也。

translations.literal: Jingmu Gong Empress Yujiulü was younger sister of Prince of Hedong Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmu Gong Empress Yujiulü was younger sister of Prince of Hedong Pi.

sentences.zh: 少以才，選入東宮。

translations.literal: In youth for talent she was chosen into the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: In youth for talent she was chosen into the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 有寵，生文成皇帝而薨。

translations.literal: She won favor, bore Wencheng, and died.
translations.idiomatic: She won favor, bore Wencheng, and died.

sentences.zh: 文成即位，追尊號諡，葬雲中金陵，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: When Wencheng took the throne, posthumous title and honorific were raised; buried at Jinling in Yunzhong; paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencheng took the throne, posthumous title and honorific were raised; buried at Jinling in Yunzhong; paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 又文成乳母常氏，本遼西人，因事入宮，乳帝，有劬勞保護之功。

translations.literal: Also Wencheng's wet-nurse Lady Chang, originally of Liaoxi, entered the palace through circumstances, nursed the emperor, and had toil in protecting him.
translations.idiomatic: Also Wencheng's wet-nurse Lady Chang, originally of Liaoxi, entered the palace through circumstances, nursed the emperor, and had toil in protecting him.

sentences.zh: 文成即位，尊為保太后，尋尊為皇太后，告于郊廟。

translations.literal: When Wencheng took the throne, she was honored as Protecting Empress Dowager, soon Grand Empress Dowager, announced at suburban temples.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencheng took the throne, she was honored as Protecting Empress Dowager, soon Grand Empress Dowager, announced at suburban temples.

sentences.zh: 和平元年，崩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Heping she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Heping she died.

sentences.zh: 詔天下大臨三日，諡曰昭。

translations.literal: An edict ordered great mourning throughout the realm for three days; posthumous title Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered great mourning throughout the realm for three days; posthumous title Zhao.

sentences.zh: 葬于廣寧磨笄山，俗謂之鳴雞山，太后遺志也。

translations.literal: Buried at Mojishan in Guangning—commonly called Cock-crow Mountain—the empress dowager's last wish.
translations.idiomatic: Buried at Mojishan in Guangning—commonly called Cock-crow Mountain—the empress dowager's last wish.

sentences.zh: 依惠太后故事，別立寢廟，置守陵二百家，樹碑頌德。

translations.literal: Following Empress Dowager Hui's precedent, a separate sleeping temple was set up; two hundred families guarded the tomb; a stele praised virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Following Empress Dowager Hui's precedent, a separate sleeping temple was set up; two hundred families guarded the tomb; a stele praised virtue.

sentences.zh: 文成文明皇后馮氏，長樂信都人也。

translations.literal: Wencheng Civilizing Empress Feng was a man of Xindu in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng Civilizing Empress Feng was a man of Xindu in Changle.

sentences.zh: 父朗，秦、雍二州刺史、西城郡公。

translations.literal: Father Lang, Inspector of Qin and Yong provinces, Duke of Xicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Father Lang, inspector of Qin and Yong provinces, Duke of Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 母樂浪王氏。

translations.literal: Mother Lady Wang of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: Mother Lady Wang of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 後生于長安，有神光之異。

translations.literal: The empress was born at Chang'an; there was a divine light anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was born at Chang'an; there was a divine light anomaly.

sentences.zh: 朗坐事誅，后遂入宮。

translations.literal: Lang was condemned and executed; the empress then entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Lang was condemned and executed; the empress then entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 太武左昭儀，后之姑也，雅有母德撫養教訓。

translations.literal: Taiwu's left zhaoyi, the empress's aunt, had motherly virtue in nurturing and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu's left zhaoyi, the empress's aunt, had motherly virtue in nurturing and instruction.

sentences.zh: 年十四，文成踐極，以選為貴人，后立為皇后。

translations.literal: At fourteen Wencheng took the throne; by selection she became noble lady; later established empress.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen Wencheng took the throne; by selection she became noble lady; later established empress.

sentences.zh: 文成崩，故事國有大喪，三日後御服器物一以燒焚，百官及中宮皆號泣而臨之。

translations.literal: When Wencheng died, by precedent on great state mourning, after three days rear-garment utensils were all burned; officials and inner palace all wept and attended.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencheng died, by precedent on great state mourning, after three days rear-garment utensils were all burned; officials and inner palace all wept and attended.

sentences.zh: 后悲叫自投火，左右救之，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: The empress wailed and threw herself into the fire; attendants saved her; after long while she revived.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wailed and threw herself into the fire; attendants saved her; after a long while she revived.

sentences.zh: 獻文即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xianwen took the throne, she was honored Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianwen took the throne, she was honored grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 丞相乙渾謀逆，獻文年十二，居於諒闇，太后密定大策，誅渾，遂臨朝聽政。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yi Hun plotted rebellion; Xianwen was twelve, in the mourning hut; the empress dowager secretly fixed the great plan, executed Hun, and then held court and heard government.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yi Hun plotted rebellion; Xianwen was twelve, in the mourning hut; the empress dowager secretly fixed the great plan, executed Hun, and then held court and heard government.

sentences.zh: 及孝文生，太后躬親撫養。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen was born, the empress dowager personally nurtured him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen was born, the empress dowager personally nurtured him.

sentences.zh: 是後罷令不聽政事。

translations.literal: Afterward she ceased orders and did not hear government.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward she ceased orders and did not hear government.

sentences.zh: 太后行不正，內寵李弈，獻文因事誅之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's conduct was improper; she favored Li Yi inwardly; Xianwen because of the affair executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's conduct was improper; she favored Li Yi inwardly; Xianwen because of the affair executed him.

sentences.zh: 太后不得意，遂害帝。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was displeased and then harmed the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was displeased and then harmed the emperor.

sentences.zh: 承明元年，尊曰太皇太后，復臨朝聽政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengming she was honored Supreme Empress Dowager and again held court and heard government.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming she was honored supreme empress dowager and again held court and heard government.

sentences.zh: 后性聰達。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was intelligent and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was intelligent and penetrating.

sentences.zh: 自入宮掖，粗學書計；

translations.literal: From entering the palace she roughly learned writing and reckoning;
translations.idiomatic: From entering the palace she roughly learned writing and reckoning;

sentences.zh: 及登尊極，省決萬機。

translations.literal: on reaching supreme rank she decided the myriad tasks.
translations.idiomatic: on reaching supreme rank she decided the myriad tasks.

sentences.zh: 孝文詔罷鷹師曹，以其地為太后立報德佛寺。

translations.literal: Xiaowen ordered the hawk-master corps abolished; its land was made Repaying Virtue Buddha Temple for the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen ordered the hawk-master corps abolished; its land was made Repaying Virtue Buddha Temple for the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后與孝文游于方山，顧川阜有終焉之志。

translations.literal: The empress dowager with Xiaowen toured Fangshan; looking at the river hills she had a will to end there.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager with Xiaowen toured Fangshan; looking at the river hills she had a will to end there.

sentences.zh: 因謂群臣曰：「舜葬蒼梧，二妃不從，豈必遠祔山陵，然後為貴哉？

translations.literal: She told the ministers: "Shun was buried at Cangwu; the two consorts did not follow—must one attach far tombs to be honored?
translations.idiomatic: She told the ministers, "Shun was buried at Cangwu; the two consorts did not follow—must one attach far tombs to be honored?

sentences.zh: 吾百歲後，神其安此。

translations.literal: After my hundred years, let my spirit rest here."
translations.idiomatic: After my hundred years, let my spirit rest here."

sentences.zh: 」孝文乃詔有司營建壽陵于方山，又起永固石室，將終為清廟焉。

translations.literal: Xiaowen then ordered authorities to build the longevity tomb at Fangshan; also the Yonggu stone chamber, to be finally a pure temple.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen then ordered authorities to build the longevity tomb at Fangshan; also the Yonggu stone chamber, to be finally a pure temple.

sentences.zh: 太和五年起作，八年而成，刊石立碑，頌太后功德。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe construction began; in the eighth year it was completed; stone was carved and a stele set praising the empress dowager's merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe construction began; in the eighth year it was completed; stone was carved and a stele set praising the empress dowager's merit.

sentences.zh: 太后以帝富於春秋，乃作《勸戒歌》三百餘章，又作《皇誥》十八篇，文多不載。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because the emperor was in spring years, composed more than three hundred chapters of Admonition Songs, also eighteen chapters of Imperial Admonitions—most texts are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager, because the emperor was in spring years, composed more than three hundred chapters of Admonition Songs, also eighteen chapters of Imperial Admonitions—most texts are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 太后立文宣王廟于長安，又立思燕佛圖于龍城，皆刊石立碑。

translations.literal: The empress dowager set up Prince Wenxuan's temple at Chang'an; also the Siyan Buddha image at Longcheng—both carved stone and set steles.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager set up Prince Wenxuan's temple at Chang'an; also the Siyan Buddha image at Longcheng—both carved stone and set steles.

sentences.zh: 太后又制，內屬五廟之孫、外戚六親緦麻，皆受復除。

translations.literal: The empress dowager also decreed: inner five-temple grandsons and outer six-kin in mourning dress all received mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager also decreed: inner five-temple grandsons and outer six-kin in mourning dress all received mourning leave.

sentences.zh: 性儉素，不好華飾，躬御縵繪而已。

translations.literal: Frugal and plain, she did not love ornament; she personally wore only coarse silk.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and plain, she did not love ornament; she personally wore only coarse silk.

sentences.zh: 宰人上膳，案裁徑尺，羞膳滋味，減於故事十分之八。

translations.literal: When stewards presented food, the tray was only a foot across; delicacies were reduced to eight-tenths of precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When stewards presented food, the tray was only a foot across; delicacies were reduced to eight-tenths of precedent.

sentences.zh: 太后嘗以體不安，服庵閭子，宰人昏而進粥，有蜒在焉，后舉匕得之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager once was unwell and took anluzi; the steward at dusk brought porridge—there was a maggot in it; the empress raised her spoon and got it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager once was unwell and took anluzi; the steward at dusk brought porridge—there was a maggot in it; the empress raised her spoon and got it.

sentences.zh: 帝時侍側，大怒，將加極罰，太后笑而釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor was then attending; greatly angered, he would impose extreme punishment; the empress dowager smiled and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then attending; greatly angered, he would impose extreme punishment; the empress dowager smiled and released him.

sentences.zh: 自太后臨朝專政，孝文雅性孝謹，不欲參決；

translations.literal: From the empress dowager's holding court and monopolizing government, Xiaowen by nature was filial and cautious and did not wish to join in decisions;
translations.idiomatic: From the empress dowager's holding court and monopolizing government, Xiaowen by nature was filial and cautious and did not wish to join in decisions;

sentences.zh: 事無巨細，一稟于太后。

translations.literal: great or small, all was reported to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: great or small, all was reported to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后多智，猜忍，能行大事；

translations.literal: The empress dowager was very clever, suspicious and cruel, able to do great deeds;
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was very clever, suspicious and cruel, able to do great deeds;

sentences.zh: 殺戮賞罰，決之俄頃，多有不關帝者。

translations.literal: killing, rewarding, and punishing were decided in a moment, many not involving the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: killing, rewarding, and punishing were decided in a moment, many not involving the emperor.

sentences.zh: 是以威福兼作，震動內外。

translations.literal: Thus might and favor together shook inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Thus might and favor together shook inside and outside.

sentences.zh: 故杞道德、王遇、張祐、苻承祖等拔自微閹，歲中而至王公。

translations.literal: Therefore Qi Daode, Wang Yu, Zhang You, Fu Chengzu and others were raised from humble eunuchs; within the year they reached kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Qi Daode, Wang Yu, Zhang You, Fu Chengzu and others were raised from humble eunuchs; within the year they reached kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 王睿出入臥內，數年便為宰輔。

translations.literal: Wang Rui went in and out of the sleeping quarters; in several years he was chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui went in and out of the sleeping quarters; in several years he was chief minister.

sentences.zh: 賞齎千萬億計，金書鐵券，許以不死之詔。

translations.literal: Rewards of tens of millions and billions, gold writ on iron tallies, a decree promising deathlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards of tens of millions and billions, gold writ on iron tallies, a decree promising deathlessness.

sentences.zh: 李沖以器能受任，亦由見寵幃幄，密加錫齎，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Li Chong for capacity received office, also from favor in the curtain; secretly bestowed gifts beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong for capacity received office, also from favor in the curtain; secretly bestowed gifts beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 后性嚴明，假有寵侍，亦無所縱。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was strict and bright; even if there were favored attendants, she did not indulge them.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was strict and bright; even if there were favored attendants, she did not indulge them.

sentences.zh: 左右纖介之愆，動加棰楚，多至百餘，少亦數十。

translations.literal: Attendants' minute faults were beaten with the rod—often more than a hundred, at least several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants' minute faults were beaten with the rod—often more than a hundred, at least several tens.

sentences.zh: 然性不宿憾，尋亦待之如初；

translations.literal: Yet she did not harbor old resentment; soon she treated them again as at first;
translations.idiomatic: Yet she did not harbor old resentment; soon she treated them again as at first;

sentences.zh: 或因此更加富貴，是以人人懷於利欲，至死而不思退。

translations.literal: or because of this they gained greater wealth—thus everyone clung to profit's desire and to death did not think of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: or because of this they gained greater wealth—thus everyone clung to profit's desire and to death did not think of retreat.

sentences.zh: 太后曾與孝文幸靈泉池，宴群臣及蕃國使人、諸方渠帥，各令為其方舞。

translations.literal: The empress dowager once with Xiaowen visited Lingquan Pool, feasting ministers and foreign envoys and chieftains of all regions, each ordered to dance his region's dance.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager once with Xiaowen visited Lingquan Pool, feasting ministers and foreign envoys and chieftains of all regions, each ordered to dance his region's dance.

sentences.zh: 孝文上壽，太后忻然作歌，帝亦和歌，遂命群臣各言其志，於是和歌者九十人。

translations.literal: Xiaowen offered longevity; the empress dowager gladly made song; the emperor also harmonized; then ordered ministers each to speak his aim—in all ninety harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen offered longevity; the empress dowager gladly made song; the emperor also harmonized; then ordered ministers each to speak his aim—in all ninety harmonized.

sentences.zh: 太后外禮人望，元丕、遊明根等頒賜金帛輿馬；

translations.literal: Outwardly the empress dowager treated men of renown; Yuan Pi, You Minggen and others received gold, silk, carriages, and horses;
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly the empress dowager treated men of renown; Yuan Pi, You Minggen and others received gold, silk, carriages, and horses;

sentences.zh: 每至褒美睿等，皆引丕參之，以示無私。

translations.literal: whenever she praised Rui and the rest she brought in Pi to show no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: whenever she praised Rui and the rest she brought in Pi to show no partiality.

sentences.zh: 又自以過失，懼人議己，小有疑忌，便見誅戮。

translations.literal: Also from her own faults, fearing others' criticism, at slight suspicion she saw execution.
translations.idiomatic: Also from her own faults, fearing others' criticism, at slight suspicion she saw execution.

sentences.zh: 迄后之崩，孝文不知所生。

translations.literal: Until the empress dowager's death, Xiaowen did not know who bore him.
translations.idiomatic: Until the empress dowager's death, Xiaowen did not know who bore him.

sentences.zh: 至如李䐶、李惠之徒，猜嫌覆滅者十餘家，死者數百人，率多枉濫，天下冤之。

translations.literal: As for Li Yi, Li Hui and the like, more than ten houses were destroyed by suspicion; the dead numbered several hundred—mostly wrongful; the realm resented it.
translations.idiomatic: As for Li Yi, Li Hui and the like, more than ten houses were destroyed by suspicion; the dead numbered several hundred—mostly wrongful; the realm resented it.

sentences.zh: 十四年，崩於太和殿，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year she died in Taihe Hall, age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year she died in Taihe Hall, age forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 其日有雄雉集于太華殿。

translations.literal: That day a male pheasant perched on Taihua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That day a male pheasant perched on Taihua Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝酌飲不入口五日，毀慕過禮。

translations.literal: The emperor drank but did not put food in his mouth for five days; mourning exceeded ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drank but did not put food in his mouth for five days; mourning exceeded ritual.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文明太皇太后。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Civilizing Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Civilizing Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 葬于永固陵，日中而反，虞于鑒玄殿。

translations.literal: Buried at Yonggu Tomb; at noon she returned; yu at Jianxuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Buried at Yonggu Tomb; at noon she returned; yu at Jianxuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: The edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The edict said:

sentences.zh: 尊旨從儉，不申罔極之痛；

translations.literal: Honoring the will for frugality, not extending unbounded grief;
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the will for frugality, not extending unbounded grief;

sentences.zh: 稱情允禮，仰損儉訓之德；

translations.literal: according with feeling and permitting ritual, upward reducing frugal instruction's virtue;
translations.idiomatic: according with feeling and permitting ritual, upward reducing frugal instruction's virtue;

sentences.zh: 進退思惟，倍用崩感。

translations.literal: advancing and retreating in thought, doubly using collapse's feeling.
translations.idiomatic: advancing and retreating in thought, doubly using collapse's feeling.

sentences.zh: 又山陵之節，亦有成命；

translations.literal: Also the mountain tomb's regulations had a fixed command;
translations.idiomatic: Also the mountain tomb's regulations had a fixed command;

sentences.zh: 內則方丈，外裁奄坎。

translations.literal: inside one zhang square, outside cut to a cubit.
translations.idiomatic: inside one zhang square, outside cut to a cubit.

sentences.zh: 脫於孝子之心有所不盡者，室中可二丈，墳不得過三十步。

translations.literal: If the filial son's heart has what is not fully done, the chamber may be two zhang; the mound must not exceed thirty paces.
translations.idiomatic: If the filial son's heart has what is not fully done, the chamber may be two zhang; the mound must not exceed thirty paces.

sentences.zh: 今以陵萬世所仰，復廣為六十步。

translations.literal: Now because the tomb is looked to for ten thousand generations, it is again broadened to sixty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Now because the tomb is looked to for ten thousand generations, it is again broadened to sixty paces.

sentences.zh: 孤負遺旨，益以痛絕！

translations.literal: Alone I have failed the last will—grief increases to cutting off!
translations.idiomatic: Alone I have failed the last will—grief increases to cutting off!

sentences.zh: 其幽房大小，棺槨質約，不設明器。

translations.literal: The inner chamber's size, coffin and inner coffin's plain quality—no bright vessels set.
translations.idiomatic: The inner chamber's size, coffin and inner coffin's plain quality—no bright vessels set.

sentences.zh: 至於素帳縵茵瓷瓦之物，亦皆不置。

translations.literal: As for plain curtains, coarse mats, and ceramic tiles, these too are not placed.
translations.idiomatic: As for plain curtains, coarse mats, and ceramic tiles, these too are not placed.

sentences.zh: 此則遵先志，從冊令。

translations.literal: This follows the former will and obeys the book's command.
translations.idiomatic: This follows the former will and obeys the book's command.

sentences.zh: 俱奉遺事，而有從有違，未達者或以致怪。

translations.literal: All following the last affairs, some followed and some violated—those who did not reach may have been startled.
translations.idiomatic: All following the last affairs, some followed and some violated—those who did not reach may have been startled.

sentences.zh: 梓宮之裏，玄堂之內，聖靈所憑，已一一奉遵，仰昭儉德。

translations.literal: Within the inner coffin, the dark hall—where the sage spirit rests—each has been followed and obeyed, showing frugal virtue upward.
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner coffin, the dark hall—where the sage spirit rests—each has been followed and obeyed, showing frugal virtue upward.

sentences.zh: 其餘外事，有所不從，以盡痛慕之情。

translations.literal: The rest, outer affairs not followed, to exhaust painful longing's feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The rest, outer affairs not followed, to exhaust painful longing's feeling.

sentences.zh: 其宣示遠近，著告群司，上明儉誨之美，下彰違命之失。

translations.literal: Proclaim far and near, set forth to all offices, above showing frugal instruction's beauty, below showing disobedience to command's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim far and near, set forth to all offices, above showing frugal instruction's beauty, below showing disobedience to command's fault.

sentences.zh: 及卒哭，孝文服衰，近臣從服。

translations.literal: At end of weeping, Xiaowen wore mourning; close ministers followed in dress.
translations.idiomatic: At end of weeping, Xiaowen wore mourning; close ministers followed in dress.

sentences.zh: 三司以下外臣衰服者，變服就練；

translations.literal: Three ministers and below, outer ministers in mourning dress changed to practice dress;
translations.idiomatic: Three ministers and below, outer ministers in mourning dress changed to practice dress;

sentences.zh: 七品以下，盡除即吉。

translations.literal: seventh grade and below removed all and returned to auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: seventh grade and below removed all and returned to auspicious.

sentences.zh: 設附祭於太和殿，公卿以下始親公事。

translations.literal: Attached sacrifice was set at Taihe Hall; dukes and below began to attend to public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Attached sacrifice was set at Taihe Hall; dukes and below began to attend to public affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝毀瘠，絕酒肉不御者三年。

translations.literal: The emperor wasted away; he abstained from wine and meat for three years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wasted away; he abstained from wine and meat for three years.

sentences.zh: 初，帝孝于太后，乃于永固陵東北里餘營壽宮，遂有終焉瞻望之志。

translations.literal: At first the emperor was filial toward the empress dowager; east of Yonggu Tomb more than a li he built a longevity palace and had a will to gaze finally.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor was filial toward the empress dowager; east of Yonggu Tomb more than a li he built a longevity palace and had a will to gaze finally.

sentences.zh: 及遷洛陽，乃自表瀍西以為山園之所，而方山虛宮號曰萬年堂云。

translations.literal: When he moved the capital to Luoyang, he himself memorialized west of the Chan for the mountain garden's place; the Fangshan empty palace was called Wannian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When he moved the capital to Luoyang, he himself memorialized west of the Chan for the mountain garden's place; the Fangshan empty palace was called Wannian Hall.

sentences.zh: 文成元皇后李氏，梁國蒙縣人，頓丘王峻之妹也。

translations.literal: Wencheng Yuan Empress Li was a man of Meng in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng Yuan Empress Li was a man of Meng in Liang.

sentences.zh: 后之生也，有異于常。

translations.literal: At the empress's birth there was something unusual.
translations.idiomatic: At the empress's birth there was something unusual.

sentences.zh: 父方叔，恆言此女當大貴。

translations.literal: Father Fangshu always said this girl would be greatly honored.
translations.idiomatic: Father Fangshu always said this girl would be greatly honored.

sentences.zh: 及長，姿質美麗。

translations.literal: When grown, bearing and quality were beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, bearing and quality were beautiful.

sentences.zh: 太武南征，永昌王仁出壽春，軍至后宅，因得后。

translations.literal: When Taiwu campaigned south, Prince of Yongchang Ren went out to Shouchun; the army reached the empress's home and thus obtained the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu campaigned south, Prince of Yongchang Ren went out to Shouchun; the army reached the empress's home and thus obtained the empress.

sentences.zh: 及仁鎮長安，遇事誅，后與其家人送平城宮。

translations.literal: When Ren guarded Chang'an, because of an affair he was executed; the empress with her family was sent to Pingcheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren guarded Chang'an, because of an affair he was executed; the empress with her family was sent to Pingcheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 高祖登白樓望見，美之。

translations.literal: Gaozu ascended the White Tower and saw her—he admired her beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ascended the White Tower and saw her—he admired her beauty.

sentences.zh: 乃下臺，后得幸於齋庫中，遂有娠。

translations.literal: He descended the tower; the empress won favor in the fasting storehouse and became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: He descended the tower; the empress won favor in the fasting storehouse and became pregnant.

sentences.zh: 常太后後問后，知之，時守庫者亦私書於壁記之，別加驗問，皆符同。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Chang later questioned the empress and knew it; the storekeeper also privately wrote on the wall and recorded it; separate added interrogation—all matched.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Chang later questioned the empress and knew it; the storekeeper also privately wrote on the wall and recorded it; separate added interrogation—all matched.

sentences.zh: 及生獻文，拜貴人。

translations.literal: When she bore Xianwen, she was made noble lady.
translations.idiomatic: When she bore Xianwen, she was made noble lady.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，太后令依故事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai'an, the empress dowager ordered according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tai'an, the empress dowager ordered according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 令后具條記在南兄弟，及引所結宗兄洪之，悉以付託。

translations.literal: She had the empress fully list brothers in the south and the sworn clan brother Hong she had joined—all were entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: She had the empress fully list brothers in the south and the sworn clan brother Hong she had joined—all were entrusted.

sentences.zh: 臨決，每一稱兄弟，拊胸慟泣，遂薨。

translations.literal: At the parting, each time she named a brother she beat her breast and wept bitterly; then she died.
translations.idiomatic: At the parting, each time she named a brother she beat her breast and wept bitterly; then she died.

sentences.zh: 后諡曰元皇后，葬金陵，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Yuan Empress; buried at Jinling; paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Yuan Empress; buried at Jinling; paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 獻文思皇后李氏，中山安喜人，南郡王惠之女也。

translations.literal: Xianwen Si Empress Li was a man of Anxi in Zhongshan, daughter of Prince of Nanjun Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen Si Empress Li was a man of Anxi in Zhongshan, daughter of Prince of Nanjun Hui.

sentences.zh: 姿德婉淑，年十八。

translations.literal: Bearing and virtue gentle and fine, age eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing and virtue gentle and fine, age eighteen.

sentences.zh: 以選入東宮。

translations.literal: By selection she entered the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: By selection she entered the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 獻文即位，為夫人，生孝文帝。

translations.literal: When Xianwen took the throne, she was lady; she bore Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianwen took the throne, she was lady; she bore Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 皇興三年，薨，葬金陵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangxing she died; buried at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangxing she died; buried at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 承明元年，追崇號諡，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengming posthumous title and honorific were raised; paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming posthumous title and honorific were raised; paired sacrifice at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 孝文貞皇后林氏，平涼人也。

translations.literal: Xiaowen Zhen Empress Lin was a man of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen Zhen Empress Lin was a man of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 父勝，位平涼太守。

translations.literal: Father Sheng, post Pingliang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Father Sheng, post Pingliang prefect.

sentences.zh: 叔父金閭，起自閹官。

translations.literal: Uncle Jinlü rose from eunuch office.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Jinlü rose from eunuch office.

sentences.zh: 獻文初，為定州刺史，為乙渾所誅，及勝兄弟皆死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianwen he was Inspector of Dingzhou; executed by Yi Hun; Sheng and brothers all died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianwen he was inspector of Dingzhou; executed by Yi Hun; Sheng and brothers all died.

sentences.zh: 勝無子，有二女入掖庭。

translations.literal: Sheng had no sons; two daughters entered the rear apartments.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had no sons; two daughters entered the rear apartments.

sentences.zh: 后容色美麗，得幸于孝文，生皇子恂。

translations.literal: The empress's bearing was beautiful; she won Xiaowen's favor and bore the prince Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's bearing was beautiful; she won Xiaowen's favor and bore the prince Xun.

sentences.zh: 以恂將為儲貳，太和七年，后依舊制薨。

translations.literal: Because Xun would be heir, in the seventh year of Taihe the empress died by the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xun would be heir, in the seventh year of Taihe the empress died by the old system.

sentences.zh: 帝仁恕不欲襲前事，而稟文明太后意，故不果行。

translations.literal: The emperor was humane and did not wish to follow the former affair, but followed Civilizing Empress Dowager's intent—thus it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was humane and did not wish to follow the former affair, but followed Civilizing Empress Dowager's intent—thus it was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 諡曰貞皇后，葬金陵。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Zhen Empress; buried at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Zhen Empress; buried at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 及恂以罪賜死，有司奏追廢后為庶人。

translations.literal: When Xun was ordered to die for crime, the authorities memorialized to posthumously depose the empress as commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun was ordered to die for crime, the authorities memorialized to posthumously depose the empress as commoner.

sentences.zh: 孝文廢皇后馮氏，太師熙之女也。

translations.literal: Xiaowen's deposed Empress Feng was daughter of Grand Tutor Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen's deposed Empress Feng was daughter of Grand Tutor Xi.

sentences.zh: 太和十七年，孝文既終喪，太尉元丕等表以長秋未建，六宮無主，請正內位。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe, when Xiaowen had ended mourning, Grand Marshal Yuan Pi and others memorialized that the chief autumn was not yet set and the six palaces had no master—please rectify the inner place.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Taihe, when Xiaowen had ended mourning, Grand Marshal Yuan Pi and others memorialized that the chief autumn was not yet set and the six palaces had no master—please rectify the inner place.

sentences.zh: 孝文從之，立后為皇后，恩遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Xiaowen followed; he established the empress; favor was very thick.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen followed; he established the empress; favor was very thick.

sentences.zh: 孝文后重引后姊昭儀至洛，稍有寵，后禮愛漸衰。

translations.literal: Xiaowen later brought the empress's elder sister zhaoyi to Luoyang; she gradually won some favor; the empress's loving courtesy gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen later brought the empress's elder sister zhaoyi to Luoyang; she gradually won some favor; the empress's loving courtesy gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 昭儀自以年長，且前入宮掖，素見待念，輕后而不率妾禮。

translations.literal: The zhaoyi, because she was older and had earlier entered the palace, was always treated with thought; she slighted the empress and did not follow concubine ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The zhaoyi, because she was older and had earlier entered the palace, was always treated with thought; she slighted the empress and did not follow concubine ritual.

sentences.zh: 后雖性不妒忌，時有愧恨之色。

translations.literal: Though the empress was not jealous by nature, at times she had a look of shame and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Though the empress was not jealous by nature, at times she had a look of shame and resentment.

sentences.zh: 照儀規為內主，譖構百端，尋廢后為庶人。

translations.literal: The zhaoyi schemed to be inner mistress; slander in a hundred ways—soon the empress was deposed as commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The zhaoyi schemed to be inner mistress; slander in a hundred ways—soon the empress was deposed as commoner.

sentences.zh: 后貞謹有德操，遂為練行尼，後終於瑤光佛寺。

translations.literal: The empress was chaste, careful, and of moral conduct; she became a practicing nun at Yaoguang Buddhist Temple and ended there.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was chaste, careful, and of moral conduct; she became a practicing nun at Yaoguang Buddhist Temple and ended there.

sentences.zh: 孝文幽皇后亦馮熙女。

translations.literal: Xiaowen You Empress was also Feng Xi's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen You Empress was also Feng Xi's daughter.

sentences.zh: 母曰常氏。

translations.literal: Mother was Lady Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Mother was Lady Chang.

sentences.zh: 本賤微，得幸於熙，熙元妃公主薨後，遂主家事。

translations.literal: Originally base and slight, she won Xi's favor; after the primary consort princess died, she then managed the household.
translations.idiomatic: Originally base and slight, she won Xi's favor; after the primary consort princess died, she then managed the household.

sentences.zh: 生后與北平公夙。

translations.literal: She bore the empress and Prince of Beiping Su.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the empress and Prince of Beiping Su.

sentences.zh: 文明太皇太后欲家世貴寵，乃簡熙二女，俱入掖庭，時年十四。

translations.literal: Civilizing Grand Empress Dowager wished the clan honored; she chose two of Xi's daughters; both entered the rear apartments, age fourteen then.
translations.idiomatic: Civilizing Grand Empress Dowager wished the clan honored; she chose two of Xi's daughters; both entered the rear apartments, age fourteen then.

sentences.zh: 其一早卒。

translations.literal: One died early.
translations.idiomatic: One died early.

sentences.zh: 后有姿媚，偏見愛幸。

translations.literal: The empress had charm and was especially loved.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had charm and was especially loved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，疾病。

translations.literal: Before long, illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, illness.

sentences.zh: 太后乃遣還家為尼，帝猶留念焉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager sent her home to be a nun; the emperor still kept her in mind.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sent her home to be a nun; the emperor still kept her in mind.

sentences.zh: 歲余而太后崩，帝服終，頗存訪之。

translations.literal: After more than a year the empress dowager died; when the emperor ended mourning, he greatly sought her.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the empress dowager died; when the emperor ended mourning, he greatly sought her.

sentences.zh: 又聞后素疹痊除，遣閹官雙三念璽書勞問，遂迎赴洛陽。

translations.literal: Also hearing the empress's chronic rash was cured, he sent eunuch Shuang Sannian with imperial writ to comfort and ask; then welcomed her to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Also hearing the empress's chronic rash was cured, he sent eunuch Shuang Sannian with imperial writ to comfort and ask; then welcomed her to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及至，寵愛過本初。

translations.literal: When she arrived, favor exceeded the first time.
translations.idiomatic: When she arrived, favor exceeded the first time.

sentences.zh: 當夕，宮人稀復進見。

translations.literal: That evening palace people rarely again entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: That evening palace people rarely again entered audience.

sentences.zh: 拜為左昭儀，後立為皇后。

translations.literal: She was made left zhaoyi; later established empress.
translations.idiomatic: She was made left zhaoyi; later established empress.

sentences.zh: 帝頻歲南征，后遂與中官高菩薩私亂。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned south year after year; the empress then privately disordered with palace eunuch Gao Pusa.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor campaigned south year after year; the empress then privately disordered with palace eunuch Gao Pusa.

sentences.zh: 及帝在汝南不豫，后便公然醜恣，中常侍雙蒙等為其心腹。

translations.literal: When the emperor was unwell at Ruyang, afterward she openly was shameless; Palace Regular Attendant Shuang Meng and others were her intimate confidants.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was unwell at Ruyang, afterward she openly was shameless; Palace Regular Attendant Shuang Meng and others were her intimate confidants.

sentences.zh: 是時彭城公主，宋王劉昶子婦也，年少嫠居。

translations.literal: At the time Princess of Pengcheng, daughter-in-law of Song Prince Liu Chang, was young and widowed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Princess of Pengcheng, daughter-in-law of Song Prince Liu Chang, was young and widowed.

sentences.zh: 北平公馮夙，后之周母弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Beiping Feng Su was the empress's younger uterine brother.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Beiping Feng Su was the empress's younger uterine brother.

sentences.zh: 后求婚于孝文，孝文許之。

translations.literal: The empress asked marriage of Xiaowen; Xiaowen assented.
translations.idiomatic: The empress asked marriage of Xiaowen; Xiaowen assented.

sentences.zh: 公主志不願，后欲強之，婚有日矣。

translations.literal: The princess's will was unwilling; the empress wished to force it—the wedding had a day.
translations.idiomatic: The princess's will was unwilling; the empress wished to force it—the wedding had a day.

sentences.zh: 公主密與侍婢及僮從十餘人，乘輕車，冒霖雨，赴懸瓠，奉謁孝文，自陳本意。

translations.literal: The princess secretly with maidservants and bond servants more than ten persons took a light carriage, braved pouring rain, went to Xuanhuai, paid homage to Xiaowen, and stated her original intent.
translations.idiomatic: The princess secretly with maidservants and bond servants more than ten persons took a light carriage, braved pouring rain, went to Xuanhuai, paid homage to Xiaowen, and stated her original intent.

sentences.zh: 因言后與菩薩亂狀。

translations.literal: She also spoke of the empress's disorder with Pusa.
translations.idiomatic: She also spoke of the empress's disorder with Pusa.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，因駭愕，未之信，而秘匿之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was startled, did not yet believe, but kept it secret.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and was startled, did not yet believe, but kept it secret.

sentences.zh: 此後后漸憂懼。

translations.literal: After this the empress gradually grew fearful.
translations.idiomatic: After this the empress gradually grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 與母常氏求托女巫，禱厭孝文疾不起；

translations.literal: With mother Chang she sought a witch, praying Xiaowen's illness would not recover;
translations.idiomatic: With mother Chang she sought a witch, praying Xiaowen's illness would not recover;

sentences.zh: 一旦得如文明太后輔少主稱命者，賞報不貲。

translations.literal: if one day she could like Civilizing Empress Dowager assist the young lord and hold command, reward would be beyond price.
translations.idiomatic: if one day she could like Civilizing Empress Dowager assist the young lord and hold command, reward would be beyond price.

sentences.zh: 又取三牲，宮中祆祠，假言祈福，專為左道。

translations.literal: Also she took three sacrificial beasts for palace Hu worship, falsely saying to pray for blessing, devoted to heterodox ways.
translations.idiomatic: Also she took three sacrificial beasts for palace Hu worship, falsely saying to pray for blessing, devoted to heterodox ways.

sentences.zh: 母常或自詣宮中，或遣侍婢與相報答。

translations.literal: Mother Chang sometimes went herself to the palace, or sent maidservants to answer back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Mother Chang sometimes went herself to the palace, or sent maidservants to answer back and forth.

sentences.zh: 帝至洛，執問菩薩、雙蒙等，具得情狀。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Luo, he interrogated Pusa, Shuang Meng and others; the full circumstances were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Luo, he interrogated Pusa, Shuang Meng and others; the full circumstances were obtained.

sentences.zh: 帝以疾臥含溫室，夜引后，並列菩薩等於戶外。

translations.literal: The emperor lay ill in the Warm Chamber; at night he summoned the empress and lined up Pusa and others outside the door.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lay ill in the Warm Chamber; at night he summoned the empress and lined up Pusa and others outside the door.

sentences.zh: 后臨入，令搜衣中，稱有寸刃便斬。

translations.literal: As the empress entered, he ordered search in her clothes—if there was a inch blade, cut at once.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress entered, he ordered search in her clothes—if there was an inch blade, cut at once.

sentences.zh: 后頓首泣謝，乃賜坐東楹，去御筵二丈餘。

translations.literal: The empress knocked head and wept in apology; then she was granted seat on the east pillar, more than two zhang from the imperial mat.
translations.idiomatic: The empress knocked head and wept in apology; then she was granted seat on the east pillar, more than two zhang from the imperial mat.

sentences.zh: 孝文令菩薩等陳狀，又讓后曰：「汝有妖術，可具言之。

translations.literal: Xiaowen ordered Pusa and the rest to state the case; again he reproached the empress: "You have witchcraft—state it fully."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen ordered Pusa and the rest to state the case; again he reproached the empress, "You have witchcraft—state it fully."

sentences.zh: 」后乞屏左右，有所密狀。

translations.literal: The empress begged to screen attendants—there was a secret report.
translations.idiomatic: The empress begged to screen attendants—there was a secret report.

sentences.zh: 孝文敕中常侍悉出，唯令長秋卿白整在側，取衛直刀拄之。

translations.literal: Xiaowen ordered all palace attendants out; only Chief of Autumn Bai Zheng at the side, taking guard straight blade to lean on it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen ordered all palace attendants out; only Chief of Autumn Bai Zheng at the side, taking guard straight blade to lean on it.

sentences.zh: 后猶不言。

translations.literal: The empress still did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The empress still did not speak.

sentences.zh: 孝文乃以綿堅塞整耳，自小語再三呼整，無所應，乃令后言。

translations.literal: Gaozu then stuffed Zheng's ears with cotton firmly, himself calling Zheng softly three times—no response—then ordered the empress to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then stuffed Zheng's ears with cotton firmly, himself calling Zheng softly three times—no response—then ordered the empress to speak.

sentences.zh: 事隱，人莫知之。

translations.literal: The affair was hidden; men did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was hidden; men did not know it.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃喚彭城、北海二王令入坐，言：「昔是汝嫂，今便他人，但入勿避。

translations.literal: Gaozu then summoned Princes of Pengcheng and Beihai to enter and sit, saying: "Formerly she was your sister-in-law; now she is another's—only enter, do not avoid."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then summoned Princes of Pengcheng and Beihai to enter and sit, saying, "Formerly she was your sister-in-law; now she is another's—only enter, do not avoid."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「此老嫗欲白刃插我肋上，可窮問本未，勿有所難。

translations.literal: Also he said: "This old woman wished to insert a white blade in my ribs—exhaustively ask the root; do not have difficulty."
translations.idiomatic: Also he said, "This old woman wished to insert a white blade in my ribs—exhaustively ask the root; do not have difficulty."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「馮家女不能復相廢逐，且使在宮中空坐，有心乃能自死，汝等勿謂吾猶有情也。

translations.literal: Also he said: "The Feng family's daughter cannot again be deposed and driven off; let her sit empty in the palace—if she has heart she can die herself—you must not think I still have feeling."
translations.idiomatic: Also he said, "The Feng family's daughter cannot again be deposed and driven off; let her sit empty in the palace—if she has heart she can die herself—you must not think I still have feeling."

sentences.zh: 」帝素至孝，猶以文明太后故，未行廢。

translations.literal: The emperor by nature was utmost filial; still because of Civilizing Empress Dowager he did not carry out deposition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor by nature was utmost filial; still because of Civilizing Empress Dowager he did not carry out deposition.

sentences.zh: 二王出，乃賜后辭死訣，再拜稽首涕泣。

translations.literal: The two princes left; then he granted the empress words of farewell to death; again bowing head and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes left; then he granted the empress words of farewell to death; again bowing head and weeping.

sentences.zh: 及入宮後，帝命中官有問於后，后罵曰：「我天子婦，當面對，豈令汝傳也！

translations.literal: After entering the palace the emperor ordered palace attendants to question the empress; the empress cursed: "I am the Son of Heaven's wife—I should face him—how can I let you transmit!"
translations.idiomatic: After entering the palace the emperor ordered palace attendants to question the empress; the empress cursed, "I am the Son of Heaven's wife—I should face him—how can I let you transmit!"

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，敕后母常入，示與后狀，常撻之百餘乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; he ordered the empress's mother Chang in; showed her the empress's case; Chang flogged her more than a hundred strokes then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry; he ordered the empress's mother Chang in; showed her the empress's case; Chang flogged her more than a hundred strokes then stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝尋南伐，且留京師。

translations.literal: The emperor soon campaigned south and stayed at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon campaigned south and stayed at the capital.

sentences.zh: 雖以罪失寵，而夫人嬪妾奉之如法。

translations.literal: Though she lost favor for crime, ladies and pin still served her by law.
translations.idiomatic: Though she lost favor for crime, ladies and pin still served her by law.

sentences.zh: 唯令世宗在東宮，無朝謁之事。

translations.literal: Only Shizong in the eastern palace had no court audience affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shizong in the eastern palace had no court audience affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝疾甚，謂彭城王勰曰：「後宮久乖陰德，自絕於天，吾死後可賜自盡別宮，葬以后禮，庶掩馮門之大過。

translations.literal: The emperor was very ill and told Prince of Pengcheng Xie: "The rear palace long lacked yin virtue and cut itself off from Heaven—after my death grant her to end herself in a separate palace; bury with empress ritual—perhaps to cover the Feng gate's great fault."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was very ill and told Prince of Pengcheng Xie, "The rear palace long lacked yin virtue and cut itself off from Heaven—after my death grant her to end herself in a separate palace; bury with empress ritual—perhaps to cover the Feng gate's great fault."

sentences.zh: 」帝崩，梓宮達魯陽，乃行遺詔。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the coffin reached Luyang; then the last edict was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the coffin reached Luyang; then the last edict was carried out.

sentences.zh: 北海王詳奉宣遺旨，長秋卿白整等入授后藥。

translations.literal: Prince of Beihai Xiang received and proclaimed the last will; Chief of Autumn Bai Zheng and others entered and gave the empress the drug.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Beihai Xiang received and proclaimed the last will; Chief of Autumn Bai Zheng and others entered and gave the empress the drug.

sentences.zh: 后走呼，不肯引決，曰：「官豈有此也！

translations.literal: The empress ran shouting, refusing to take resolution, saying: "How can the ruler have this!
translations.idiomatic: The empress ran shouting, refusing to take resolution, saying, "How can the ruler have this!

sentences.zh: 是此諸王輩殺我耳。

translations.literal: These kings killed me."
translations.idiomatic: These kings killed me."

sentences.zh: 」整等執持強之，乃含椒而盡。

translations.literal: Zheng and the rest held and forced her; then she took pepper and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and the rest held and forced her; then she took pepper and died.

sentences.zh: 梓宮次洛南，咸陽王禧等知審死，相視曰：「若無遺詔，我兄弟亦當作計去之。

translations.literal: When the coffin next reached south of Luo, Prince of Xianyang Xi and others knew the true death and looked at each other: "Without the last edict, we brothers would also have made a plan to remove her.
